items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I didn't relate to anything! ... I had no idea... If he said a name like Fletcher Henderson, I would know. ... Later I learned... Later that week I was up there one night... But to me it sounded a little old-timey. I didn't really appreciate what he was doing...

ctx.x: things for me, and was talking a lot of things to me that was going in one ear and out the other because it wasn't important to me. I was watching him play the piano, and these names he was calling... I didn't relate to anything! It's so funny how things like that happen. Teaching school now, I have kids that, you mention names like Lester Young or Charlie Parker or somebody to them, and they don't have no idea who you're talking about. And these can be music students. So at that particular time, I had no idea...…

Anyway, he sat down and he played for me, and I realized he played the piano very good. But to me it sounded a little old-timey. I didn't really appreciate what he was doing, but the fact that he could play just was enough for me. Later I learned... Later that week I was up there one night, and they were all standing outside, him and some other musicians, and they were into an argument. These guys were... I could see that he was arguing against everybody up there, or everybody up there was arguing against him.…
